summary: # CLO 2025 Course: Unlock New Styles in Denim ## Introduction Today, I'm going to show you how to make a cow's water wash costume. In this process, I will demonstrate how to transform a simple basic shirt into a jacket. ## Opening the CLO App First, open the CLO app. If you have downloaded the necessary materials, you can upload them to the application. I have already downloaded them in advance. You can obtain the materials by replying to the public number for the cow's water wash. ## Importing the Basic Style Shirt After opening the material, we first import a basic style shirt file. ### Style Adjustments 1. **Initial Observations:** - The shirt has a single plate at the bottom. - The door is relatively wider. - The upper body and the front body are cut up and down. - There are two vertical cuts on the lower half. - The design includes a pocket and a belt cover. 2. **Editing the Length:** - We will adjust the shirt length using the edit plate tool. - Go directly to the frame and select the bottom line of the front and back plates. - Move the whole thing up and down. - Press the right mouse button to open a window that allows you to enter a moving distance. I will enter 55 to control its length. 3. **Measuring the Total Length:** - After the change, I will measure the total length of the bottom, using the shortcut key Z for the edit plate tool. - The total length of the selected line is 638.2 mm. ### Drawing the Plate Again Next, we will use the shape tool (shortcut key S) to find the shape tool on the right. - In the blank area of the 2D window, press the button and enter 638.2 mm. - If your length changes differ from mine, measure according to my method. - Use the edit plate tool to align this plate, creating the bottom plate. ## Sewing the Pieces Together - You can use either free sewing or line sewing. - Sew the bottom and the front and back of the circle. - After sewing, navigate to the 3D window to use the adjustment plate tool to move the plate slightly. - Right-click on the plate to add it to the side, placing it near our sewing plate. ### Adding Buttons and Buttonholes - There should be a button and a buttonhole on the bottom plate, forming a set of buttons. - Refer to the position of the door frame above to add it to the bottom plate. - Select the line with the edit plate tool and ensure that the center of the door frame is the middle point. ### Positioning the Buttons - If we add a button below, it should also be 20 mm from the edge. - First, find the button tool in the 3D toolbar on the left. - Right-click on the plate to add the left button. - Set the distance between the top and bottom of the plate to the appropriate values. ## Modifying the Door Frame 1. **Widening the Door Frame:** - If you want to make the door frame wider, combine the door frame division line and draw a wider division line using the editor tool (shortcut key Z). - Select the division line together while pressing the Shift key and merge them to widen the door frame to 40 mm. 2. **Drawing Vertical Lines:** - Draw a vertical line again on the right side using the internal multi-sided line tool (shortcut key G). - Merge the sections together as needed. ## Panel Adjustments ### Front Panel Adjustments - The front panel has a hollow line in the middle. - Use the hook and loop tool to cut and sew the lines. - Adjust the curves if necessary using the edit curve tool. ## Pocket and Belt Cover Creation 1. **Drawing the Pocket:** - Use the plus point dividing tool (shortcut key X) to create the pocket version first. - The pocket version should be slightly wider than the two vertical lines. - Ensure the pocket is a closed shape. 2. **Creating the Belt Cover:** - Use similar techniques to create the cover, ensuring it is wider than the pocket. ## Final Adjustments - After completing the pocket and belt cover, use the loop tool to finalize the panels. - Sew everything together and adjust the front panel accordingly. ## Water-Washing Effects 1. **Changing Fabric Properties:** - Change the fabric type to denim and apply the appropriate water-washing effects based on the desired appearance. - Experiment with different water-washing supply types, such as plain wash, speed wash, and stone wash. 2. **Adjusting Parameters:** - Set parameters like softening, degree of integration, and duration to achieve the desired look. - Use the 3D window to visualize the effects in real-time. ## Rendering the Final Product - Once you are satisfied with the design, prepare for rendering. - Set the scene, lighting, and any additional elements you want to include. - Finally, render the model to visualize the final output. ## Conclusion By following these steps, you will have successfully created a washed denim jacket with detailed designs and a professional finish. Remember to save your work regularly and experiment with different styles and techniques to master denim in CLO.
